'''Giacomo Mauro D'Ariano''' (born 11 May 1955) is an Italian quantum physicist. He is a professor of theoretical physics at the [[University of Pavia]], where he is the leader of the QUIT ([[quantum information theory]]) group.<ref>{{cite web |title=QUIT |url=http://www.qubit.it}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Il teletrasporto passa dalla fisica quantistica |url=https://laprovinciapavese.gelocal.it/tempo-libero/2017/04/27/news/il-teletrasporto-passa-dalla-fisica-quantistica-1.15261688|date=2017-04-28}}</ref> He is a member of the Center of Photonic Communication and Computing at [[Northwestern University]];<ref name="CPCC">{{cite web |title=Center for Photonic Communication and Computing |url=https://cpcc.northwestern.edu/people/index.html}}</ref> a member of the [[Istituto Lombardo Accademia di Scienze e Lettere]]; and a member of the [[Foundational Questions Institute]] (FQXi).<ref>{{cite web |title=Curriculum vitae of GM D'Ariano |url=https://www.qubit.it/people/dariano/}}</ref>

His primary areas of research are [[Quantum information science|quantum information theory]], the mathematical structure of quantum theory, and foundational problems of contemporary physics.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Physicists Want To Rebuild Quantum Theory From Scratch |magazine=Wired|url=https://www.wired.com/story/physicists-want-to-rebuild-quantum-theory-from-scratch/|date=2017-09-02}}</ref> As one of the pioneers of quantum information theory, he has made major contributions to the informational-theoretical derivation of quantum theory.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Physics Without Physics: The Power of Information-theoretical Principles |journal=International Journal of Theoretical Physics |volume=56 |issue=1 |pages=97–128 |arxiv=1701.06309 |doi=10.1007/s10773-016-3172-y |year=2017 |last1=d'Ariano |first1=Giacomo Mauro |bibcode=2017IJTP...56...97D |s2cid=119338397 }}</ref>

== Early life and career ==

D'Ariano was born on 11 May 1955. He got Laurea cum laude in Physics in 1978 from Pavia University. In 1978, he started a research fellowship in Polymer Science at Politecnico di Milano and in 1979, a research fellowship at Pavia University. In 1984, he was appointed as research assistant at the University of Pavia and as a result of national competitions he became associate professor in 1992 and full professor in 2000.<ref>{{cite web |title=Biographical Sketch: Giacomo Mauro D'Ariano |url=http://www.qubit.it/people/dariano}}</ref>

At the time of his appointment, there were no PhD schools in Italy<ref>{{cite web |title=PhD Programs in Italy |url=https://www.findaphd.com/study-abroad/europe/phd-study-in-italy.aspx}}</ref> and D'Ariano became one of the first PhD supervisors in the country. He founded the Quantum Information Theory Group (QUIT) in 2000 and took on the role of the group leader. In the same year, he was also selected as a member of the Photonic Communication and Computing at Northwestern University.<ref name="CPCC" />

== Scientific contributions ==

=== Quantum information ===
D'Ariano and his collaborators introduced the first exact algorithm for quantum homodyne tomography of states,<ref>{{cite journal |title=Detection of the density matrix through optical homodyne tomography without filtered back projection |journal=Physical Review A|volume=50|issue=5|pages=4298–4302|doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.50.4298|pmid=9911405|year=1994 |last1=d'Ariano |first1=G. M. |last2=MacChiavello|first2=C.|last3=Paris|first3=M. G. A.|bibcode=1994PhRvA..50.4298D}}</ref> and they subsequently generalized the technique used to do to a universal method of quantum measurement.<ref>{{cite book |title=Asymptotic Theory of Quantum Statistical Inference |doi=10.1142/5630|year=2005 |last1=Hayashi |first1=Masahito |isbn=978-981-256-015-5}}</ref> D'Ariano then developed the first experimental scheme—now called "ancilla-assisted tomography"—that made the characterization of quantum channels, operations, and measuring apparatuses feasible to be actually done in the laboratory, by exploiting a single entangled input state.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Quantum tomography for measuring experimentally the matrix elements of an arbitrary quantum operation. |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=86 |issue=19 |pages=4195–8 |pmid=11328133 |year=2001 |last1=d'Ariano |first1=G. M. |last2=Lo Presti |first2=P. |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.86.4195 |arxiv=quant-ph/0012071 |bibcode=2001PhRvL..86.4195D |s2cid=119075753 }}</ref>

D'Ariano proposed [[quantum entanglement]] as a tool for improving the precision of quantum measurement,<ref>{{cite journal |title=Using Entanglement Improves the Precision of Quantum Measurements |journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=87|issue=27|article-number=270404|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.87.270404|pmid=11800863|year=2001 |last1=d'Ariano |first1=G. Mauro |last2=Lo Presti|first2=Paoloplacido|last3=Paris|first3=Matteo G. A.|arxiv=quant-ph/0109040|s2cid=11199855}}</ref> an idea that, parallel to works of other authors, suggested the new field of [[Quantum metrology]]. He has also introduced several new types of measurement. With his team, he solved a number of long-standing problems of quantum information theory, such as the optimal broadcasting of mixed states;<ref>{{cite journal |title=Superbroadcasting of Mixed States |journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=95|issue=6|article-number=060503|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.95.060503|pmid=16090933|year=2005 |last1=d'Ariano |first1=Giacomo Mauro |last2=MacChiavello|first2=Chiara|last3=Perinotti|first3=Paolo|arxiv=quant-ph/0506251|bibcode=2005PhRvL..95f0503D|s2cid=2978617}}</ref> the optimal phase-estimation for mixed states,<ref>{{cite journal |title=Optimal phase estimation for qubits in mixed states |journal=Physical Review A|volume=72|issue=4|article-number=042327|doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.72.042327|year=2005 |last1=d'Ariano |first1=Giacomo Mauro |last2=MacChiavello|first2=Chiara|last3=Perinotti|first3=Paolo|arxiv=quant-ph/0411133|bibcode=2005PhRvA..72d2327D|s2cid=117753018}}</ref> and the optimal protocols for phase cloning.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Optimal phase-covariant cloning for qubits and qutrits |journal=Physical Review A|volume=67|issue=4|article-number=042306|doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.67.042306|year=2003 |last1=d'Ariano |first1=Giacomo Mauro |last2=MacChiavello|first2=Chiara|arxiv=quant-ph/0301175|bibcode=2003PhRvA..67d2306D|s2cid=119490312}}</ref>

D'Ariano and collaborators introduced the concept of "quantum comb",<ref>{{cite journal |title=Quantum Circuit Architecture |journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=101|issue=6|article-number=060401|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.101.060401|pmid=18764438|year=2008 |last1=Chiribella |first1=G. |last2=d'Ariano|first2=G. M.|last3=Perinotti|first3=P.|arxiv=0712.1325|bibcode=2008PhRvL.101f0401C|s2cid=16160309}}</ref> which generalizes that of "quantum operation", and has a wide range of applications in optimization of quantum measurements, communication, algorithms, and protocols. He and his group subsequently used quantum combs to find the optimal apparatuses for [[Quantum tomography]].<ref>{{cite journal |title=Optimal Quantum Tomography of States, Measurements, and Transformations |journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=102|issue=1|article-number=010404|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.102.010404|pmid=19257173|year=2009 |last1=Bisio |first1=A. |last2=Chiribella|first2=G.|last3=d'Ariano|first3=G. M.|last4=Facchini|first4=S.|last5=Perinotti|first5=P.|arxiv=0806.1172|bibcode=2009PhRvL.102a0404B|s2cid=31954030}}</ref> The quantum-comb framework also enabled a new understanding of causality in quantum mechanics and quantum field theory. This understanding had a wide and diverse impact in several areas of research, beginning with the study of quantum causal interference and causal-discovery algorithms, used in recent attempts, along quantum informational lines, at reconciling quantum theory and general relativity, one of the great outstanding problems of fundamental physics.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Quantum causality |journal=Nature Physics|volume=10|issue=4|pages=259–263|doi=10.1038/nphys2930|year=2014|last1=Brukner|first1=Časlav|bibcode=2014NatPh..10..259B|s2cid=236500884 }}</ref>

=== Quantum foundations ===
D'Ariano has played a major role in making quantum information theory a new paradigm for the foundations of quantum theory and fundamental physics in general. In 2010, he proposed a set of information-theoretical postulates for a rigorous derivation of (finite-dimensional) Quantum Theory,<ref>{{cite web |title=Philosophy of Quantum Information and Entanglement |url=https://www.cambridge.org/it/academic/subjects/physics/history-philosophy-and-foundations-physics/philosophy-quantum-information-and-entanglement?format=HB}}</ref> a derivation subsequently achieved in his collaboration with Giulio Chiribella and Paolo Perinotti.<ref name=qtderiv>{{cite journal |title=Informational derivation of quantum theory |journal=Physical Review A|volume=84|issue=1|article-number=012311|doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.84.012311|year=2011 |last1=Chiribella |first1=Giulio |last2=d'Ariano|first2=Giacomo Mauro|last3=Perinotti|first3=Paolo|arxiv=1011.6451|bibcode=2011PhRvA..84a2311C|s2cid=15364117}}</ref> This project also led to a new way of understanding, working with, and developing quantum theory, presented in a comprehensive textbook entitled ''Quantum Theory from First Principles''.<ref name=QTFP>{{cite web|title=Review: Quantum Theory from First Principles|url=http://thequantumtimes.org/2017/07/review-quantum-theory-from-first-principles-g-chiribella-g-m-dariano-and-p-perinotti-cambridge-2017/|date=2017-07-12|access-date=18 December 2018|archive-date=19 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180619113248/http://thequantumtimes.org/2017/07/review-quantum-theory-from-first-principles-g-chiribella-g-m-dariano-and-p-perinotti-cambridge-2017/}}</ref>

In the mid 2010s, D'Ariano extended this program to a derivation of Quantum Field Theory from informational-theoretical postulates, which enabled him and his team to derive the complete free [[Quantum field theory]].<ref name="auto">{{cite journal |title=Derivation of the Dirac equation from principles of information processing |journal=Physical Review A|volume=90|issue=6|article-number=062106|doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.90.062106|year=2014 |last1=d'Ariano |first1=Giacomo Mauro |last2=Perinotti|first2=Paolo|arxiv=1306.1934|bibcode=2014PhRvA..90f2106D|s2cid=118385875}}</ref> In an article in [[New Scientist]], [[Lucien Hardy]] wrote that "their work and their approach is extraordinary", and Časlav Brukner wrote that he was "impressed" by their work writing that "there's something deep about quantum mechanics in this work".<ref>{{cite web |title=Quantum purity |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg22630161-100-quantum-purity-how-the-big-picture-banishes-weirdness/}}</ref>

A historical perspective, from [[Paul Dirac|Dirac]]'s discovery of [[quantum electrodynamics]] to the present time, on this work was given by Arkady Plotnitsky in The Principles of Quantum Theory, From Planck's Quanta to the [[Higgs boson|Higgs Boson]].<ref>{{cite book |title=The Principles of Quantum Theory, From Planck's Quanta to the Higgs Boson |url=https://www.springer.com/it/book/9783319320663|isbn=978-3-319-32066-3|publisher=Springer|year=2016}}</ref>
A book by Oliver Darrigol offers an extensive commentary on D'Ariano and co-workers' derivation of Quantum Mechanics, especially emphasizing how it overcomes certain ''ad hoc'' assumptions of previous derivations.<ref>{{cite book |title=Physics and Necessity |url=https://global.oup.com/academic/product/physics-and-necessity-9780198712886?cc=it&lang=en&|isbn=978-0-19-871288-6|publisher=Oxford University Press|date=2014-05-22}}</ref>

On the formulation of quantum theory based on information principles, physicist [[Federico Faggin]] based his theory on the nature of [[consciousness]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Federico Faggin. Irriducibile - Filosofia |url=https://www.raicultura.it/filosofia/articoli/2022/11/Federico-Faggin-Irriducibile--10f11b52-4e16-4b30-a8fb-200b353b933d.html |access-date=2023-04-27 |website=Rai Cultura |language=it}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==

Giacomo Mauro D'Ariano is a Fellow of the [[Optical Society of America]] and of the [[American Physical Society]]. He won the third prize for the FQXi essay world competitions of 2011,<ref>{{cite web |title=A Quantum-Digital Universe |url=https://fqxi.org/community/essay/winners/2011.1}}</ref> 2012<ref>{{cite web |title=Quantum-informational Principles for Physics |url=https://fqxi.org/community/essay/winners/2012.1}}</ref> and 2013.<ref>{{cite web |title=It From Qubit |url=https://fqxi.org/community/essay/winners/2013.1}}</ref> His paper on the informational derivation of quantum theory<ref name="qtderiv" /> has been selected for an APS Viewpoint.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Viewpoint: Questioning the rules of the game |journal=Physics|volume=4|url=https://physics.aps.org/articles/v4/55|date=2011-07-11|last1=Brukner|first1=Časlav|page=55 |doi=10.1103/Physics.4.55|doi-access=free}}</ref>
In 2022 he won, together with [[Mikhail Lukin]] ([[Harvard University]]) and [[Andreas Winter]] ([[Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona]]) the [[International Quantum Award]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Winners of the International Quantum Award 2022 |url=http://www.phys-info.org/news/winners-of-the-international-quantum-award-2022}}</ref>
